title: Rafael and the Witness
premise: When archivist Lior Almeida receives a confession letter postmarked the day after Mayor Duarte's funeral, it claims the mayor's death was murder — and names a witness the whole town buried years ago: Rafael, a boy who vanished from the cathedral crypt's locked records. As the anniversary dinner approaches, Lior discovers Rafael never died but was hidden by the cathedral itself, and that the letter-writer is someone still protecting him. The killer, now the town's beloved interim mayor, closes in on both the witness and the archivist who found him. At the anniversary dinner, Lior exposes the truth publicly, choosing love and found family over the duty of silence he has kept for twenty years.
about_author: Bram Joubert is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing small-town archives before turning to crime fiction. He writes mysteries about quiet people whose orderly lives are upended by one unfiled truth.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Lior Almeida, POV. In the cathedral archive, Lior files the last papers of Mayor Duarte's estate, establishing his meticulous, lonely routine and his quiet affection for the town's secrets. A letter arrives, postmarked the day after the funeral, claiming Duarte was murdered. Emotional beat: unease cracking open a settled life.

chapters.title: A Name Not in Any Register
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. The unsigned letter names 'Rafael' as the sole witness to the murder — but Lior's own catalogs record Rafael as dead for twenty years. He checks baptismal registers, finds pages razored out. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of realizing his archive lies.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Lior petitions the elderly sacristan, Dona Beatriz, to open the crypt sealed since his arrival as archivist; she refuses with visible fear. He notices fresh scratches on the lock. Emotional beat: the institution he serves becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: Interim
chapters.summary: Vice-Mayor Cordeiro, POV. The charming interim mayor learns of Lior's questions through a nervous clerk and begins smoothing things over — offering Lior a promotion, access, friendship. Emotional beat: menace dressed as generosity.

chapters.title: What Beatriz Buried
chapters.summary: Dona Beatriz, POV. Flashback chapter: twenty years ago, Beatriz hid a battered teenage boy in the crypt after he witnessed a fatal 'accident' involving young Cordeiro and Duarte. She falsified his death record. Emotional beat: guilt as an act of love.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Lior traces the confession letter's paper to the cathedral's own supply and its handwriting to someone trained in liturgical script — narrowing suspects to those inside the church. Someone ransacks his office overnight. Emotional beat: hunted inside a sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Town preparations for the mayor's memorial dinner reveal how deeply everyone loved Duarte — and how Cordeiro controls the narrative of Duarte's death as a heart attack. Lior meets Marta, the coroner's daughter, who doubts her father's signed report. Emotional beat: an ally found in shared doubt.

chapters.title: Scratches on the Lock
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta helps Lior examine the crypt door; the scratches are recent, made from inside. Someone is living down there — or was. They find a tin cup and a child's carved saint. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Rafael
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. In the dark under the cathedral, the man who has been Rafael for twenty years — now called Brother Anselmo by the two priests who shelter him — hears footsteps above and knows his hiding is ending. He decides, for the first time, to come up rather than be dragged out. Emotional beat: agency after decades of erasure.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Father Amaro, the old pastor, admits he wrote the letter: dying of cancer, he could no longer guard the secret alone. He gives Lior the original testimony Rafael hid in the reliquary. Emotional beat: the weight of a secret handed over.

chapters.title: The Reliquary Testimony
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. The hidden document describes Duarte and Cordeiro's embezzlement scheme and the night Cordeiro killed their accomplice while Rafael watched from the choir loft. Lior realizes the 'accident' victim was never investigated because Duarte helped bury it. Emotional beat: the town's golden history curdling.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: Cordeiro, POV. Cordeiro invites Lior personally to the anniversary dinner, having learned of the reliquary theft from a bribed clerk. He offers Lior everything he's ever lacked — belonging, recognition — if the papers disappear. Emotional beat: temptation precisely aimed at loneliness.

chapters.title: Marta's Father's Files
chapters.summary: Marta, POV. Marta confronts her dying father, who confesses he falsified the autopsy under pressure and kept Cordeiro's payments in a shoebox — including a photo proving Rafael alive in 2009. Emotional beat: filial love versus complicity.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Rafael tells Lior and Marta his story at last: how Beatriz took him in, how the priests gave him a new name, how he chose to stay hidden even when he could have fled — because leaving meant no one would remember what he saw. Emotional beat: found family forged in hiding.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. A fire guts the archive wing; the reliquary testimony is presumed destroyed, and Father Amaro is hospitalized from smoke inhalation. Lior had already smuggled the true pages out. Emotional beat: grief and cold clarity — this was attempted murder.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised Early
chapters.summary: Cordeiro, POV. Confident the evidence is ash, Cordeiro rehearses his eulogy-toast and orders discreet surveillance on Lior and Marta. His composure frays when he learns Father Amaro survived. Emotional beat: a predator discovering the trap is his own.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Beatriz, POV. Beatriz offers to turn herself in for falsifying records, begging Lior to let her carry the legal weight alone. Lior refuses: twenty years of dutiful silence protected killers, not the town. Emotional beat: duty redefined as truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The dinner begins; Cordeiro raises his glass to Duarte's memory. Lior stands, and with Marta and the recovered testimony, reads the dead accomplice's name into the record before three hundred guests. Emotional beat: the held breath before the break.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Rafael, POV. Rafael walks into the banquet hall — the man the town mourned two decades ago — and identifies Cordeiro as the killer before the assembled town. Cordeiro lunges for him; Marta and the off-duty sergeant intervene. Emotional beat: the erased name spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Head Table
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. Cordeiro, undone by the surviving testimony and the coroner's shoebox, is arrested mid-denial. The town's grief turns to reckoning; some curse Lior for shaming them, others thank him. Emotional beat: vindication that costs something.

chapters.title: Reopening the Crypt
chapters.summary: Lior and Rafael, POV. The crypt is opened lawfully at last; Beatriz surrenders to a sympathetic prosecutor, and Father Amaro, dying, asks Rafael's forgiveness — which Rafael gives. Lior and Rafael begin cataloguing the truth together, page by page. Emotional beat: tenderness after exposure.

chapters.title: Filed Under Alive
chapters.summary: Lior, POV. One year later: Rafael has a legal identity again, a small apartment above the archive, and a place at Lior's table. Lior creates a new register — not of the dead, but of the living who were almost lost. Emotional beat: love and family, finally alphabetized.
